name: Jaw is law

card.summary: A looksmaxxing framework holding that jaw quality outweighs other facial features, which directs effort toward jawline-improving routes such as leanness, grooming, orthodontics or surgery.
card.note: A community belief rather than a procedure; forum members disagree about how much weight the jaw carries versus the eye area.

quick.overview:
"Jaw is law" is a looksmaxxing slogan claiming that the jaw is the single most important feature in how attractive a face looks. Followers use it to prioritise a defined, angular jawline, whether through lower body fat, grooming, dental and orthodontic work, fillers or jaw surgery.

It is one side of a long-running forum debate: others argue that the eye area is the main feature ("eyes are the prize"). Published research on facial attractiveness covers jaw shape and chin form as part of the picture, but no study has tested the slogan itself.
quick.how: In practice the idea shapes what people work on first. Leaner faces show the jawline more, so body-fat reduction is commonly mentioned; others discuss facial hair, hairstyle and posture, orthodontics, chin or jaw implants and fillers, and orthognathic surgery. Members also use it as a lens when rating photos, judging a face mainly by the lower third.
quick.risks: The belief itself carries no physical risk. Some routes people associate with it, such as jaw surgery or implants, are medical procedures with their own risks, and others, such as hitting the face, are unsafe and covered in other articles. Community discussion of the slogan can also encourage fixation on a single feature.

lead: "Jaw is law" (jawlaw) is a phrase in looksmaxxing communities stating that jaw quality outweighs every other facial feature in determining attractiveness. It functions as a prioritisation rule: if the jaw is strong, the face reads as attractive, and if it is weak, other features cannot fully compensate.

People who hold the view use it to direct improvement work toward the lower face: reducing facial fat so the jawline shows, grooming, and in hardmaxx discussions orthodontics, implants or jaw surgery. Wikipedia's looksmaxxing article lists a defined jawline among features looksmaxxers assess [3].

The slogan is contested within the same communities, notably by those who give the eye area top priority. Research on physical attractiveness reports preferences for angular male jawlines in Western countries, but it has not tested whether the jaw outranks other features [2].

chain: Treat the jaw as the highest-priority feature
Work on leanness, grooming, dental or surgical jaw change
More defined lower face in photos and in person
angle.text: The framework steers effort to the jawline. Followers pursue visible definition through lower body fat and styling, and some discuss orthodontic or surgical options to change jaw structure.

paras: The phrase condenses a hierarchy of features into one rule. On looksmax.org it appears in thread titles such as one asserting that "few mms of bone" is real [1] and others posting photos for evaluation under the banner [4]. Opponents answer with the eye area as the deciding feature, a debate that recurs on the forum [5].

Proponents point to examples of men with strong jaws regarded as attractive despite other features, and to the idea that small differences in jaw bone make a visible difference. A forum thread cites a study in which faces judged unattractive rated higher when the lower half was masked, which the poster presents as support for the slogan [6]. Critics in the same community say eye area and other features carry equal or greater weight [5].

Wikipedia's article on physical attractiveness reports that angular male jawlines are favoured as ideal in Western countries while the ideal female jaw is rounder and softer, that men with low submental fat are viewed as having better jawlines, and that the jutting square chin is largely a European-heritage trait and not a universal marker [2]. In one study with Chinese, Malay and Indian judges, people with retrusive mandibles were rated most attractive [2]. These findings describe jaw preferences within particular samples; no study found tests a rule that the jaw outweighs all other features.

The slogan is shorthand in rating threads and a common reference when members debate hardmaxx options such as jaw surgery [3]. It sits alongside other hierarchies of features and is regularly argued against by members who rank other features first [5].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the phrase appears across many threads, mostly as an argument about whether the jaw or the eye area matters most [1][5].

claims.claim: The jaw matters more than any other feature.
claims.believers: Proponents say a strong jaw lets a face be rated highly even when other features are ordinary, and that a few millimetres of bone change how a face reads [1].
claims.experts: Research summaries report preferences for angular male jawlines in some populations but note that chin and jaw ideals vary by ethnicity and sex [2]. No study found ranks the jaw above all other features.

claims.claim: Faces look more attractive when the lower half is hidden, which shows the jaw is what drags them down.
claims.believers: A forum poster cites a study of masked faces as proof that the lower face decides attractiveness [6].
claims.experts: The study is described only in a forum thread, and no peer-reviewed source on it was located for this article.

claims.claim: The eye area, not the jaw, is the main feature.
claims.believers: Rival posters argue that raters demand strong eyes to call a face top-tier and that a face fails without them [5].
claims.experts: No published study found directly compares jaw and eye contributions as a ranking.
